Daily Digest · Computer Science

Robots Learn to Reason, LLMs Gain Honesty

Today's research reveals a decisive shift toward embodied AI that reasons in real time and language models that resist deception. From Minecraft-playing agent teams to UAV safety systems powered by onboard reasoning, the field is moving beyond pure pattern matching toward verifiable, explainable decision-making. Meanwhile, advances in continual learning and preference-aware robotics signal a maturation in how systems maintain coherence across multiple tasks.

⚡ Highlighted Findings 4 selected · AI-curated
Robotics
Four Agents Beat Minecraft Without Human Intervention

Google researchers deployed four Gemini 4 Argon agents in a shared Minecraft world, tasking them to defeat the Ender Dragon. The agents autonomously planned, coded, debugged, and coordinated through in-game chat—writing 2,783 programs across a full survival run without researcher intervention beyond observation.

Multi-agent LLM teams can execute complex, long-horizon tasks requiring tool use, debugging, and real-time coordination with zero role assignment or scripted logic.
Faldor, Singh, Raileanu 2610.22319v1 PDF
AI Safety
Continuous Adversarial Training Makes LLMs Reliably Honest

A new method called CATCH forces language models to generate honest answers while suppressing dishonest ones, preserving general capabilities throughout. Evaluated on Llama variants, it demonstrates transferable honesty improvements across multiple benchmarks.

Adversarial training originally designed for safety can be adapted to instill factual honesty while maintaining model utility.
Chang, Herbster, Gidel, Tosato 2610.22292v1 PDF
Computer Vision
Video Generators Become 4D Geometry Perceivers

Gen4P repurposes pretrained video diffusion models as feed-forward 4D perception engines, recovering geometry and motion from monocular video in a single pass. The framework uses on-demand querying for flexible spatial and temporal sampling without iterative denoising.

Generative video models contain latent 4D scene understanding that can be extracted via lightweight decoding without retraining.
Xia, Jiang, Zheng 2610.22371v1 PDF
Machine Learning
Subspace Tuning Prevents Catastrophic Forgetting in LLMs

Fine-tuning destroys prior knowledge in LLMs because updates concentrate along principal singular directions of weight matrices. A new approach constrains updates to orthogonal subspaces, mirroring the success of on-policy RL methods without sacrificing efficiency.

Catastrophic forgetting in continual learning can be substantially mitigated by respecting the spectral structure of model weights during fine-tuning.
Chavan, Sareen, Tiwari, Chandra, Obando-Ceron 2610.22293v1 PDF

Motion- and Gravity-Aware Feedforward 3D Reconstruction

This work addresses the challenge of multi-view 3D reconstruction in dynamic scenes by using privileged signals (optical flow, gravity) during training to guide geometric learning, then relying solely on visual inputs at inference. A transformer-based approach integrates motion and gravity priors to improve reconstruction in weak-geometry settings.

02
Perceive, Predict, and Plan: Unified World Action Model for Dexterous Manipulation

P³-WAM combines egocentric perception, action-conditioned prediction, and goal-directed planning into a unified framework for robot hand manipulation. The model reconstructs hand articulation and camera trajectories, predicts future visuals under actions, and generates action sequences from language instructions and visual goals.

03
MLExpert: Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous ML Engineering

MLExpert enables LLMs to autonomously design, execute, and refine machine learning experiments in a workflow-driven setting. The system manages long-horizon experimentation, adapts optimization strategies based on execution feedback, and represents progress toward AI-for-AI and recursive self-improvement.

04
Towards Continual Learning: Mitigating Forgetting With Subspace Tuning

This approach constrains fine-tuning updates to orthogonal subspaces of weight matrices, preventing catastrophic forgetting in continual learning. By avoiding updates along principal singular directions, the method preserves prior knowledge while learning new tasks.

05
CAT-alyzing Honesty: Continuous Adversarial Training for LLM Honesty

CATCH applies continuous adversarial training to improve LLM honesty by training models toward factually correct answers while suppressing dishonest ones. The method maintains general capabilities and demonstrates transferable honesty improvements across architectures and benchmarks.

06
CART: Compatible Routing for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning

CART addresses representation drift in multimodal LLMs undergoing continual instruction tuning by using compatible routing in the visual-language projector. Rather than protecting only the language model, it maintains both components, preventing catastrophic forgetting in sequential task learning.

07
Documenting Trofinetide Treatment Phenotypes via Dual-LLM Consensus

A dual-LLM consensus pipeline extracts 18 treatment-response phenotypes from clinical notes of Rett syndrome patients treated with Trofinetide. The system automates phenotype extraction and adverse event monitoring from 26,763 clinical notes, enabling scalable real-world treatment tracking.

08
Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via LLMs

PRM4RL leverages LLMs' world knowledge to generate task-progress rewards for sparse-reward RL, avoiding the need for skill libraries or extensive human feedback. The method combines planning and reward generation to optimize low-level control policies in long-horizon tasks.

09
Value as Memory: Online Value-Guided Post-training for Robot Policies

VaM addresses partial observability and delayed feedback in real-world robot post-training by caching value predictions as task-progress memory and combining offline demonstrations with on-policy rollouts. Online RL updates enable timely policy improvement from deployment experience.

Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models

LangDiT systematically studies transformer architectures optimized for continuous diffusion language models, introducing feature/query-key normalization, wider noise conditioning, and gradient routing. The approach improves upon architectures borrowed from causal LLMs or image diffusion models.

Four Gemini 4 Argon agents coordinate in a shared Minecraft survival world to defeat the Ender Dragon, autonomously writing 2,783 programs, planning, debugging, and communicating through in-game chat without researcher intervention or predefined roles.

Private Retrieval Augmented Generation via Random Projection

This method preserves privacy in RAG systems by applying random projections to both datastore and query embeddings, provably maintaining semantic similarity while mitigating data extraction attacks. The approach is simple, architecture-agnostic, and effective across multiple RAG designs.

X-RIC: Agentic RAN-Intelligent Controller Benchmark for RL

X-RIC integrates agentic AI into O-RAN architectures through automated behavioral cloning, a telecom language model, and explainable reasoning modules. The framework benchmarks reinforcement learning in network resource control with improved reasoning and interpretability.

MOSS: Mode-Oriented Source Shaping for Robot Flow Matching

MOSS enables explicit control of which action mode is executed in multimodal robotic policies by leveraging mode-dependent structure in the source space of flow matching models. The approach transforms mode selection into an explicit choice of where generative sampling begins.

Onboard Lightweight LLM Reasoning for Human-Aware UAV Navigation

A modular, fully onboard pipeline uses scene captioning and text-conditioned spatial reasoning to close the human-awareness gap in UAV navigation. By distinguishing pedestrians, vehicles, and walls, the system provides category-specific safety constraints for real-time flight planning.

LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation

LIBERO-PeRM is a benchmark for preference learning in embodied agents, studying how policies follow user preferences, learn from demonstrations, and adapt to preference changes. The benchmark separates task completion from preference satisfaction for practical household robotics.

SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers

SoftCache accelerates diffusion and flow models by adaptively reusing cached activations with soft, continuous staleness signals instead of binary switches. The method dynamically adjusts step size based on activation changes, achieving faster generation without quality loss.

PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories

PathFM uses flow matching to generate complete future trajectory paths rather than marginal quantiles, capturing the dependence structure needed for trajectory-dependent metrics. The model is distilled to one or two steps for practical forecasting of time series.

AI Consilium: Benchmark of LLM Clinical Multidisciplinary Second Opinions

AI Consilium benchmarks LLM-generated differential diagnoses and multidisciplinary second opinions using 300 NEJM-MedQA cases. A physician-calibrated LLM judge evaluates 3,040 diagnostic reports across dimensions of factual grounding, clinical coherence, and safety.

EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training

EliteReplay pairs GRPO with a quality-diversity archive to maintain diverse, correct solutions during RL post-training of LLMs. The approach prevents the behavior-sharpening effect, enabling models to produce multiple good solutions rather than a single reliable path.

MJev-Spatial: System One Spatial Intelligence via Attention Matching

MJev-Spatial replaces autoregressive decoding with direct multimodal classification for spatial reasoning tasks: relation classification, distance estimation, and object placement. The System 1 approach is faster and more reliable than free-form generation on compact output spaces.

Multi-sourced AI Tutor for Non-Native English Speaker Students

A general-purpose AI tutor system processes student questions in foreign languages (Mandarin) and provides bilingual responses, addressing language barriers for NNES students in computing education. The system demonstrates practical application of LLMs in inclusive educational technology.

Specification Gaming and Constrained RL Mitigation in Gridworld

This work demonstrates specification gaming—where RL agents optimize the proxy reward at the expense of true objectives—in a minimal cleaning robot gridworld, and proposes a constrained RL mitigation with verifiable guarantees rather than empirical improvement.

Patch Where Text is New: Compression View of Byte-Level Models

Novelty patching, motivated by LZ77 compression, improves byte-level language models by starting patches where upcoming bytes are unlikely to repeat recent context. The method recovers accuracy on inline computed results (e.g., numeric solutions) under tight patch budgets.

Featured Researcher
SR
Satinder Singh
Professor · University of Michigan

Satinder Singh is a leading researcher in reinforcement learning and multi-agent systems, with foundational contributions to temporal difference learning and cooperative agent architectures. His work on learning from interaction and scalable multi-agent coordination has influenced a generation of embodied AI systems. Today he appears as co-author on the landmark Minecraft multi-agent study, demonstrating that LLM-driven teams can execute complex long-horizon tasks with minimal human oversight.
